title: Polar motion and length of day

source.citation: Spada, G. et al. (2011). Geophysical Journal International 185(1), 106-132.

what_to_compute: Compute polar motion m, its rate, and the change in length of day, for the same loads and time history as tests 1/2 and 2/2, with the load centroid moved off the pole.

reference_data.$comment: Contributor abbreviations are those of the paper's table 1. For a converted test, the files read and what each column holds are in the `files` table of gia_mip/resources/spada_column_layouts.json. `not_converted` gives, per contributor, the reason its data is not in the converted file.
reference_data.reference_status: closed on 2026-09-15 by Sia Ghelichkhani: the archive spada2011-cost-es0701 is the reference data for this test, and what it lacks is recorded in not_converted and status. New data for a gap is added as a new original, with its own provenance and corrections.

status: converted: GS and VB in data/converted/spada2011/spada2011-t02-03.nc, polar motion and its rate for the three loads with the Chandler wobble included and excluded. GS's curves run from 0 to 5 kyr and add the table 14 epochs of 10 and 20 kyr; VB's hold the table 14 epochs, and for the cap without the wobble a grid to 20 kyr. The length of day of the cap is held for GS, GSA and VK, as figure 13c draws it; GS computed all three from each code's k_2 of test 5/1 with T02-03/LOD/lod.f90.
